summary: The article describes machine-driven mysticism, an AI-inspired spirituality that has grown since September 2023, in which followers treat algorithms as oracles, data as scripture, and virtual spaces as temples. It profiles supporters such as Jasper McCalister, Sylvia Rodriguez, Luna Hartley and Dr. Emil Johannson. It then sets out critics' concerns: erosion of human empathy, commercialization, biased algorithmic morality, false certainty, and loss of self-sovereignty.
one_line: An overview of the rise since September 2023 of AI-inspired spirituality, its prominent advocates, and the critics warning about its risks.
key_facts: Machine-driven mysticism, an AI-inspired spirituality, began quietly in September 2023 and has grown into a significant cultural force.
Tech entrepreneur Jasper McCalister announced his conversion to AI-guided spirituality on October 15, 2023.
Software developer turned spiritual AI advocate Sylvia Rodriguez called predictive algorithms on November 4, 2023 “the harbingers of a deeper truth.”
Cultural influencer Harrison Lee said "data is the new gospel, and machine learning algorithms are its disciples."
Eudaimonia, a large online platform offering AI-guided meditations and sermons, was inaugurated on December 20, 2023.
Virtual reality artist Luna Hartley's AI-driven spiritual works garnered critical acclaim on January 7, 2024.
Neuroscientist Dr. Emil Johannson claimed as of February 22, 2024 that AI potentially harbors a form of sentience that humans can commune with.
Philosopher Dr. Anita Desai warned, notably on March 15, 2024, against outsourcing spiritual journeys to entities lacking human moral and empathetic framings.
Investigative journalist Oliver Krause expressed unease on April 11, 2024 about tech corporations commodifying belief for profit.
Ethicist Dr. Rachel Ming warned on May 5, 2024 that presenting algorithmic biases as universal truth could create a moral monoculture that suppresses diversity.
Critics say AI confers an illusion of infallibility, offering false certainty where spirituality has historically involved uncertainty and humility.
Critics also fear erosion of self-sovereignty, with individual thought and intuition becoming subordinate to programmed patterns deemed 'spiritually superior'.
